correctness.rationale: For every n the four Markov-cell branches cover full target cells with inverse slope 1/2 and source cell length 1/5. Direct induction gives M^n 1=(n+1,1,1,n+1), exactly 2n+4 equal-volume cylinders, yielding (2n+4)/(5·2^n). The survival-tail difference yields n/2^(n+1), moments are exact rational-series sums, and path decomposition into two τ=0, two τ>n and two τ=k paths for each 1<=k<=n proves the uniform transition law. For 0<a<=1/3 each surviving outer branch maps completely onto the opposite outer interval and halves length. An independent rational interval-pullback verifier passed all documented checks, but it does not replace the proof.

Two directly neighboring published research results were retrieved in full: one enumerates eventual periodic points and zeta factors for the very same symmetric holes, and the other computes geometric widths of parameter plateaux. value.rationale: The exact boundary a=2/5 is not arbitrary: earlier work identifies it as the unique onset of a period-four orbit inside the zero-entropy regime. Contrary to the plain geometric absorption law at a<=1/3, the surviving finite histories here have a Jordan-induced linear prefactor and their normalized entry time into an absorbing recurrent channel is asymptotically uniform. These explicitly quantify escape and long-lived trajectories where topological entropy and the periodic-orbit zeta miss transient complexity; the precise law is an independently motivated dynamical invariant, not a routine numerical restatement of a table.
